question: Who is the Chief Election Commissioner of India as of November 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunil Arora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sunil Arora served as the Chief Election Commissioner of India from **December 2, 2018, to April 12, 2021**.
 
• He succeeded Om Prakash Rawat and was succeeded by Sushil Chandra.
 
• During his tenure, Sunil Arora oversaw the 2019 General Elections in India, one of the largest democratic exercises in the world.
 
• Arora had a distinguished career in the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) before his appointment as the Chief Election Commissioner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The ECI is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It was established on January 25, 1950, to ensure free and fair elections in the country.
 
• The commission is composed of a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners.
 
• ECI’s major functions include the preparation of electoral rolls, supervision of elections, and ensuring the implementation of the model code of conduct.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)**
 
 
• The CEC is the head of the Election Commission of India and is responsible for ensuring elections are conducted impartially and fairly.
 
• The CEC is appointed by the President of India and usually has a tenure of six years or up to the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CEC can only be removed from office in a manner similar to the removal of a Supreme Court judge, that is through a process of impeachment by Parliament.
 
 
 
• **2019 General Elections in India**
 
 
• The 2019 General Elections were held in seven phases from April 11 to May 19, 2019.
 
• It was the largest democratic exercise in the world, with around 900 million eligible voters.
 
• The elections resulted in a victory for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led by Narendra Modi.
